summary: Closes FIND-M9-70-SERVICES-TABLE-STRING-MATCH. SessionsService::list_sessions tolerated a missing 'sessions' table by substring-matching the store error text (contains("does not exist")); after m9-70 the store returns Ok(vec![]) for that case, so the branch was unreachable dead code that could also mask an unrelated store failure whose message happened to contain those words. The service now propagates the store error verbatim, and the 'no sessions yet' case is documented as a store contract at the call site. No observable behavior change post-m9-70: the existing list_sessions_empty test is promoted from vacuous to load-bearing, which is proved by reverting the store-side absent-table handling and watching it fail.
title: 71 services list store contract

subject.gap: chronos-services::sessions::list_sessions recovered from a missing sessions table by string-matching the rendered store error (err_str.contains("does not exist") || err_str.contains("not exist")), then handed the matched path Ok(ListResult { sessions: vec![] }). Two defects in one line of policy: it keys off a human-readable message instead of redb's typed TableError::TableDoesNotExist, and after m9-70 made the store return Ok(vec![]) for a virgin database it became unreachable for its only intended case. Living dead code that would silently swallow a genuine store error whose text happened to contain 'not exist'.
subject.fix: list_sessions now propagates the store error verbatim (ctx.store.list_sessions().map_err(|e| ServiceError::ListFailed(e.to_string()))?) and its doc comment states that 'no sessions yet' is a store contract, not a caller concern. The removed comment claimed a missing table 'returns an empty list, suitable for empty stores' from the service layer; that responsibility now sits only in chronos-store. list_sessions_empty gained a doc comment recording that it is load-bearing precisely because the workaround is gone, plus the falsification procedure that demonstrates it.

deferred.note: crates/chronos-store/src/storage.rs::load_session handles the absent-table case with a wildcard, Err(_) => StoreError::SessionNotFound(...), in both read paths, while list_sessions and session_exists (same file, same concern, same commit in m9-70) match redb::TableError::TableDoesNotExist explicitly. The wildcard is harmless today (open_table on a read transaction realistically only fails with TableDoesNotExist), but it documents nothing and would misreport a future redb error variant as 'session not found'. Decide whether to make the three read paths agree on the explicit match. No behavior change today; no test can currently distinguish the two forms.
